plan.estimand: Main effect of the 2-level factor in a balanced 3-by-2 fixed factorial ANOVA, tested with 1 numerator degree of freedom against the residual error
plan.hypothesis: H₀: no main effect of the 2-level factor (all cell means are equal when pooled across the 3-level factor); H₁: at least one contrast among the 2 levels differs across the factor levels
assumptions: Balanced design: equal sample size n per cell across all 6 cells (3 × 2 = 6)
Fixed factor ANOVA model with both factors fixed
Independent observations within and across cells
Responses are normally distributed within each cell
Homogeneity of variance: common population variance σ² across all 6 cells
All cell means are estimated (no structural constraints); the tested main effect involves 1 numerator degree of freedom
Partial eta-squared (η²_p) = 0.06 represents the effect size for the 2-level factor main effect
The test is two-sided at α = 0.05, assessing whether the 2-level factor has a non-zero main effect
scientific_notes: Partial eta-squared is converted to the non-centrality parameter λ for the F-distribution via: λ = (η²_p / (1 − η²_p)) × df_error, where df_error = 6(n − 1) in a 3×2 balanced design with n per cell
The F-test has numerator df = 1 (the 2-level factor main effect) and denominator df = 6(n − 1) (residual error with 6 cells and n observations per cell)
Power calculation uses the non-central F-distribution F(1, 6(n−1), λ) to find the minimum n such that P(F > F_{crit}) ≥ 0.80, where F_{crit} is the critical value at α = 0.05

target_power <- 0.80
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
num_levels_factor_A <- 3
num_levels_factor_B <- 2
num_cells <- num_levels_factor_A * num_levels_factor_B  # 6 cells
df_numerator <- 1  # Main effect of the 2-level factor
target_power_check <- 0.80

# Critical value for the F-test at alpha = 0.05 with df_num = 1
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = Inf)

# Function to compute power given n (participants per cell)
compute_power <- function(n) {
  df_error <- num_cells * (n - 1)
  
  # Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter
  # lambda = (eta_p^2 / (1 - eta_p^2)) * df_error
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq / (1 - partial_eta_sq)) * df_error
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit) where F ~ F(df_num, df_error, lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Binary search for minimum n

n_max <- 500

while (n_max - n_min > 1) {
  n_mid <- (n_min + n_max) %/% 2
  power_mid <- compute_power(n_mid)

plan.hypothesis: H₀: no main effect of the 2-level factor (all cell means are equal when pooled across the 3-level factor); H₁: at least one contrast among the 2 levels differs across the factor levels
assumptions: Balanced design: equal sample size n per cell across all 6 cells (3 × 2 = 6)
Fixed factor ANOVA model with both factors fixed
Independent observations within and across cells
Responses are normally distributed within each cell
Homogeneity of variance: common population variance σ² across all 6 cells
All cell means are estimated (no structural constraints); the tested main effect involves 1 numerator degree of freedom
Partial eta-squared (η²_p) = 0.06 represents the effect size for the 2-level factor main effect
The test is two-sided at α = 0.05, assessing whether the 2-level factor has a non-zero main effect
scientific_notes: Partial eta-squared is converted to the non-centrality parameter λ for the F-distribution via: λ = (η²_p / (1 − η²_p)) × df_error, where df_error = 6(n − 1) in a 3×2 balanced design with n per cell
The F-test has numerator df = 1 (the 2-level factor main effect) and denominator df = 6(n − 1) (residual error with 6 cells and n observations per cell)
Power calculation uses the non-central F-distribution F(1, 6(n−1), λ) to find the minimum n such that P(F > F_{crit}) ≥ 0.80, where F_{crit} is the critical value at α = 0.05

  df_error <- num_cells * (n - 1)
  
  # Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter
